newsitem.title: USA: Exxon says U.K. approves 3 natgas fields.
newsitem.headline: Exxon says U.K. approves 3 natgas fields.

text.p: Exxon Corp said on Thursday that the British government approved plans to develop three high-pressure, high-temperature natural gas condensate fields in the Central North Sea with combined reserves of one billion barrels of oil equivalent.

Exxon said its United Kingdom affiliate, Esso Exploration & Production Ltd, has an overall interest of about 105 million oil equivalent barrels in the developments, which also involve nine other co-ventures. The fields are in 295 feet of water about 150 miles east of Aberdeen, Scotland.
It said production is due to come onstream in mid-2000.

The Shearwater field will be operated by Royal Dutch/Shell Group and the Elgin and Franklin fields will be operated by Elf Aquitaine. They will be developed via two separate central-processing facilities at a total cost of $3.5 billion, including drilling, Exxon said.
Natural gas will be exported through a jointly owned, $600 million, 300-mile pipeline to the existing Shell/Exxon plant at Bacton, England, from where it can reach British or European markets.
Production from both projects is expected to be up to 900 million cubic feet of natural gas per day and 240,000 barrels per day of liquids, the company said.

The fields pose significant technical challenges due to high pressure and high temperature. The reservoirs are 16,000 feet or more below the seabed. Exxon said the operators have developed technologically advanced facilities to handle these conditions, using their own expertise and also that of Exxon and other co-venturers.
